summary: Kazuo Oyamada is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University from around 1970 to 1974 and held a post at Rissho University from circa 1987 to 2018.
Kazutoshi Soma works in Buddhist studies. He studied under Meiji Yamada and served as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Kazuyoshi Hotta focuses on Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, where he was also attested as a manager in 2007, and served as a fixed-term assistant professor at Otani University in 2015.

Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1942–1948). He founded Shinnyokai and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and Chicago (PhD under Mircea Eliade), lectured at Brown (~1960–1964), and became Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA, serving ~1967–1994.

Kei Kataoka specializes in Indology and philosophy. Educated at the University of Tokyo and National Sanskrit University, he held posts at Wolfson College, Oxford, the University of Tokyo, Fukuoka University, and Kyushu University, where he became a professor.
Kei Okusa is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in literature from Otani University, where he is attested as a faculty member in 2026.

Keiichi Miyamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara, earning a literature doctorate, and held positions at Kokugakuin University as lecturer (1986), associate professor (1988), and professor (1995).

Keiji Iwata (1922–2013) worked in religious studies and other fields. After studying at Kyoto University (~1942–1945), he held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1969–1980) and Otani University (~1986–1993).
Keiji Kokubu (1907–1997) was a philosopher who studied at Ryukoku University (~1928–1931) under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku University, Nanzan University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a Kyoto School philosopher who studied under Nishida, Tanabe, and Heidegger at Kyoto University and Freiburg. He held a lectureship at Otani University (~1928–1935) and served as professor at Kyoto University (1943–1964).

Keiki Nakayama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Kyoto University, he served as a JSPS DC2 fellow (2020) and as a visiting scholar at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Tohoku Gakuin, Taisho, and the University of Tokyo, he founded Miwa Gakuin and held teaching posts at Taisho University, Shukyo University, and the University of Tokyo.

Keikyo Nakamikado is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015).
Keinin Hayashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has served as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute and was formerly a lecturer at Waseda University.

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD at Durham University (~2007–2011) under Robin Coningham. He held academic posts at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) and La Trobe University (2016).

Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He taught at Koyasan University (1959–1973; 2005–2009) and served as a professor at Kochi University (~1965–1995).

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He served as professor at Rissho University and Tohoku University, and later as president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1993–1998).

Keisuke Fujii is an architectural historian and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held positions there from 1982 to 2018, rising to professor, and served as visiting professor at Tokyo University of the Arts.
